fields.title: HLS Basics
fields.description: Learn how to segment an MP4 into HLS chunks, build an .m3u8 playlist, and serve it in a player.

fields.title: What is HLS?
fields.explanation: HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) was created by Apple. It splits video into small .ts segments (typically 2–10 seconds) and provides a playlist file (.m3u8) that tells the player which segments to fetch in order. Because it's served over plain HTTP, it works through CDNs and firewalls that block RTMP.

fields.title: Segment a video into HLS
fields.explanation: The `-hls_time 6` flag sets each segment to ~6 seconds. `-hls_list_size 0` keeps all segments in the playlist (VOD mode). The output is `playlist.m3u8` plus numbered `.ts` files.
fields.command: ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -hls_time 6 -hls_list_size 0 -hls_segment_filename segment_%03d.ts playlist.m3u8
fields.command_description: Transcode MP4 → H.264/AAC, split into 6-second segments, write HLS playlist
fields.expected_output_hint: You should see segment_000.ts, segment_001.ts ... and playlist.m3u8 in the output files.

fields.title: Inspect the .m3u8 playlist
fields.explanation: A Media Playlist lists every segment with its duration. The #EXT-X-TARGETDURATION tag tells the player the max segment length. #EXT-X-ENDLIST marks a complete (VOD) stream. Copy the playlist.m3u8 URL from the output and paste it into the Player Lab to verify playback.
fields.command_description: Print total duration parsed from the HLS playlist
fields.expected_output_hint: A number in seconds representing total stream duration.

fields.title: Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) Ladder
fields.description: Create multiple quality renditions and a master playlist so players can switch bitrates based on network conditions.

fields.title: What is ABR?
fields.explanation: Adaptive Bitrate Streaming (ABR) encodes the same video at multiple resolutions/bitrates. A Master Playlist lists all renditions. The player measures download speed and buffer health, then switches to the best-fitting rendition automatically. This is what powers Netflix, YouTube, and every major OTT platform.

fields.title: Encode 720p rendition
fields.explanation: Create the 720p tier at ~2.5 Mbps video, ~128k audio. `-maxrate` and `-bufsize` constrain peaks for CBR-like delivery over HTTP.

fields.title: Encode 360p rendition
fields.explanation: The 360p low-quality tier is critical for users on weak connections. At ~500 kbps it still delivers watchable video.

fields.title: Codec Comparison: H.264 vs H.265 vs AV1
fields.description: Transcode the same clip to three codecs and compare file size versus quality. Understand why newer codecs exist.

fields.title: Why do codecs matter?
fields.explanation: A codec compresses raw video frames. Better codecs = same quality at lower bitrate = less storage, less bandwidth, faster streams. H.264 (AVC) is the universal baseline. H.265 (HEVC) is ~40% smaller at the same quality. AV1 is royalty-free and ~50% smaller than H.264, but encodes much slower.

fields.title: Encode with H.264 (CRF 23)
fields.explanation: CRF (Constant Rate Factor) controls quality. 0 = lossless, 51 = worst. 23 is the default and a good baseline. Lower = better quality + larger file.
fields.command: ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 23 -preset medium -c:a aac -b:a 128k output_h264.mp4
fields.command_description: H.264 encode at CRF 23, medium preset

fields.title: Encode with H.265 (CRF 28)
fields.explanation: H.265 at CRF 28 produces roughly the same visual quality as H.264 at CRF 23, but the file is ~40% smaller. The encode is slower. Note: not all browsers support H.265 natively (needs hardware decode or MSE).
fields.command: ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v libx265 -crf 28 -preset medium -c:a aac -b:a 128k output_h265.mp4
fields.expected_output_hint: output_h265.mp4 should be noticeably smaller than H.264 output.

fields.title: Encode with AV1 (CRF 30)
fields.explanation: AV1 is royalty-free (developed by Alliance for Open Media). At CRF 30 it matches H.265 quality at ~10-20% smaller size. Encoding is very slow (libaom-av1). For production use SVT-AV1 which is 20-50x faster.
fields.expected_output_hint: output_av1.mp4. Smallest file. Encoding will take significantly longer.

fields.title: FFmpeg Filters Essentials
fields.description: Learn the filtergraph system: scale, crop, overlay, drawtext, and audio normalization.

fields.title: Scale and pad for a standard size
fields.explanation: The `scale` filter resizes video. `scale=-2:1080` sets height to 1080px while keeping aspect ratio (width rounded to multiple of 2 for codec compatibility). The `pad` filter adds black bars to hit an exact dimension (letterbox).
fields.expected_output_hint: output_1080p.mp4 at exactly 1920x1080 with letterbox bars if needed.

fields.title: Burn a timecode overlay
fields.explanation: `drawtext` writes text on each frame. `%{pts\:hms}` is the PTS (Presentation Timestamp) formatted as HH:MM:SS — useful for QC review copies.
fields.command_description: Burn HH:MM:SS timecode into top-left corner
fields.expected_output_hint: output_timecode.mp4 with white timecode stamp on each frame.

fields.title: Audio loudness normalization (EBU R128)
fields.explanation: OTT platforms require audio at -23 LUFS (EBU R128) or -24 LUFS (ATSC A/85). The `loudnorm` filter auto-normalizes integrated loudness, true peak, and LRA in a single pass.
fields.command_description: Normalize audio to EBU R128 (-23 LUFS), copy video stream
fields.expected_output_hint: output_normalized.mp4 with corrected loudness. Check with ffprobe or a LUFS meter.
